Mysteria noctu peragebantur: videtur ergo aemulatio quaedam fuisse, quis maximam facem accederet: quod Graeci dicunt ἀᾶδα ἱστάναι. quasi statuere & defigere ad lucendum. Plutarchus in Cicerone & ὁ φῶς πολλὰ καλέλαμπε τὲς ἑνωπὰς, λαμπάδια καὶ ἀᾶδας ἱσώλων ἐπὶ τῆ Σύρας. inde apud scriptores saepe ἀᾶδυχεῖν & μυσηρία. & placet veteribus Grammaticis ἀᾶδυχεῖν proprie dici de eo qui fit daduchus in Eleusiniis initiis. Fuerunt & alia λαμπαδυχίας certamina varia Athenis, ut praeter Platonem, Paufaniam in Atticis, & Suidam, scholiastes Aristophanis docet: sed id aliud, ut puto, erat. Quanquam quod ait μεγίςλω, putauimus aliquando eo pertinere, quod videtur in eiusmodi agonibus fuisse aliquod virium corporis specimen. Ait enim Comicus in Ranis, λαμπάδα δ' ἐδεῖς οἵος τε φέρειν ὑπ' ἀγυμνασίας ἔτι νῦν. & Andocides in oratione quadam inter καταφρώματα fua numerat, quòd λαμπαδῆν εἴχνοτε. Sed de mysteriorum facibus passim veteres.

page.notes: The scan is small and the Greek is hard to read in places; the Greek passages are the most likely to contain errors and are not checked letter by letter. The small-type annotations sit inside the column and are transcribed as running text. A stray mark at the bottom left (a dot and a small stroke) is ignored as not printed text. The last line "cebant," stands alone at the right and is taken as the completion of "exer-", so it is not treated as a catchword.
